For those who don't realize how impressive this is, I'm going to use Arcane Odyssey as an example.

When you're in the Dark Seas or Bronze Seas doing ship combat, you'd have to stop your ship to go fight NPCs because due to the fact that if your ship keeps running and you jump, you fly off backwards. That's normal roblox physics, when your vehicle is running forwards and you jump, the vehicle kind of "outspeeds" you and leaves you behind.

With Rell Seas custom physics, this means you can fight on ships while it's running. So your friends who man the wheel and cannons can keep shooting at other ships in the distance, while you kick enemies off your ship deck. This alone opens up the possibility to escape ships when they surround you. With other ship combat from other games, you'd have to stop your ship and defeat everybody around you if you want to live.

Not only that, but this also allows you to chill out or move around the ship without being at the helm.

@YS-Madara I guess they could, I think either way is fine, but I do prefer 3 per server and here is why:

RELL Seas is a game with lots of servers, of course. Because of this, the position of Admiral will be almost irrelevant to anyone who isn't highly ranked on the leaderboard. This is because it just doesn't have any effect on almost anyone at all.

What are the odds of you meeting 1 of 3 of the top ranked Marine players in the game? If you really didn't want to meet them to avoid a fight, you could easily log off and just not deal with the Admirals.

Obviously, the Admiral rank wouldn't just be whoever is the most powerful Marine, since that would mean when the game starts, the first Marine to get to level 2 is an Admiral. There would be a minimum requirement.


The 3 Admirals per game would work if the servers were big enough that the amount of them would be in the single digits. That way, it would be really common to have an Admiral in your server. That would make Admirals have a bigger impact on the servers as a whole, since they could really just show up on the spot.

But we both know that having servers in the single digits isn't possible with it would affect performance, which is why 3 Admirals per server would probably be best.

Why RELL Seas Will Surpass Blox Fruits
For years, Blox Fruits has dominated the Roblox One Piece-inspired game scene. But with the arrival of RELL Seas, that reign might be coming to an end. This isn’t just hype—there are clear, logical reasons why RELL Seas has the potential to overtake Blox Fruits in both quality and popularity.

1. Years of Development and Planning
RELL Games has dedicated 5 to 6 years to developing RELL Seas. This long development cycle allowed the team to refine gameplay systems, balance mechanics, and ensure the world feels alive. In contrast, Blox Fruits evolved over time through frequent but often repetitive updates, focusing more on content quantity than overall design depth.

2. A Truly Massive World
The RELL Seas map is huge, with dozens of islands, hidden locations, and deep-sea environments. One of its standout features is submarine exploration—allowing players to dive beneath the waves and discover underwater cities, treasure, and dangers. Blox Fruits doesn’t offer this level of vertical exploration, sticking mostly to surface-level travel.

3. Depth Beyond Grinding
Where Blox Fruits often falls into the loop of “fight NPCs, move to next island, repeat,” RELL Seas expands player activities:

Cooking & Restaurants – Players can craft meals with unique effects and even run a restaurant.

Fishing & Hunting – Earn rewards through peaceful or dangerous activities.

Dynamic World Events – Ghost ship attacks, sea beast encounters, and random treasure hunts keep gameplay fresh.

4. Advanced Combat & Haki System
Combat in RELL Seas is highly customizable:

Multiple fighting styles: swords, guns, martial arts, and more.

Haki upgrades and variations allow for personalized strategies.

God Fruits with unique abilities for both PvP and PvE scenarios.
Unlike Blox Fruits, which often encourages spamming the strongest skill, RELL Seas rewards skillful timing, combos, and adaptability.

5. Visuals and Immersion
RELL Seas uses modern Roblox development
